acceptance_criteria: AC-1 With no eligible credential, both the manual and the discovery selector offer the inline creation control.
AC-2 With the credential list in error, both paths still offer the control, and the error is still shown.
AC-3 Creating a credential from the discovery path makes it selectable there without reopening the dialog.
AC-4 The helper text no longer directs the operator elsewhere when the dialog itself can create one.
AC-5 The two selectors do not duplicate the control's markup, or the SESSION_CLOSE says why they must.
AC-6 npx vitest run passes with the new tests, npx tsc --noEmit is clean, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_13G_LOCAL_IDENTITY_ADMINISTRATION_AND_CLI_PARITY.md -- FROZEN. Inline credential creation from the add-device dialog shipped under it; this movement does not add a capability, it makes an existing one reachable from the second place that needs it.
baseline.engineering_baseline: The dialog already holds the inline creation state and renders the creation surface; only one of the two selectors exposes the control that opens it.
baseline.product_baseline: An operator adds a device either by typing an address or by importing a discovered candidate. Both paths require a credential reference. Reported by the Product Owner on 2026-09-15, on the discovery path: the dialog said no stored credential allows Check Point and offered no way to create one.
baseline.test_baseline: npx vitest run and npx tsc --noEmit pass on origin/main today, run locally on 2026-09-15 before this packet was written. They pass because no test covers the discovery path's credential selector.

invariants: No credential value, secret or password is rendered, logged or placed in a test fixture.
The eligibility rule -- which credential may be used for which vendor -- is unchanged.
Both paths behave identically with respect to creating a credential; that identity is the point of the movement.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Let an operator create a credential from wherever the dialog asks for one. The add-device dialog has two credential selectors -- one on the manual path and one on the discovery path -- and only the manual one offers the Create credential button. An operator importing a discovered candidate is told to go to the Credentials tab instead, on the same screen where the manual path would have let them create one inline. The button is also hidden whenever the credential list fails to load, which is precisely when an operator most needs a way forward.
output_contract: An operator who needs a credential can make one where they are standing, on either path.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One control and one helper text, on a path that already has the state and the surface it needs.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
The two frontend commands run from ui2/frontend; the privacy gate runs from the repository root.
Run only the commands named above. Do not run the Java build.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before every commit and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE says whether you unified the two selectors or kept them separate, and quotes the new helper text.
risks: Copying the block a second time, which leaves two places to keep in step and reproduces this defect on the next change.
Showing the control on error but leaving the selector disabled, so the operator creates a credential and still cannot pick it.
Touching the eligibility filter while unifying the two selectors, which would change a flow that works.

in: The discovery path's credential selector offers the same inline creation control the manual path already offers, opening the same surface and using the same state.

The control is no longer suppressed when the credential list failed to load. A failed list is exactly when an operator has no way forward, and telling them to use a tab they may not be able to load either is not a way forward. Keep showing the error; show the control as well.
The helper text stops sending the operator to the Credentials tab when the very same dialog can create one. Say what is true: none of the stored credentials allows this vendor, and offer the control.

Prefer removing the duplication over copying the block a second time: if the two selectors can share one component or one rendered fragment, do that, so the next change cannot land on one path and miss the other. If they genuinely cannot, say why in the SESSION_CLOSE.

Tests: the control is present on both paths when no eligible credential exists; it is present when the credential list failed to load; creating a credential from the discovery path selects it and lets the flow continue.
out: Any change to credential creation itself, to its API, or to what a credential may hold.
Any change to the vendor-to-credential eligibility filtering.
Any change to the discovery flow beyond the credential selector.
Any new route or service change. This is entirely in the dialog.
